review_notes: I read the whole target file and the definition of `addDirichletUnit` and its simp lemma `sum_addDirichletUnit` in Dirichlet/ParameterShift.lean. I grepped the library for pointwise evaluation lemmas for `addDirichletUnit` and found none. `addDirichletUnit` is a plain `def` over `Function.update`, so it is not reducible. I found no loop, competing-rule or orientation problem in this file. The `by simpa using add_pos ...` calls and the other local simp uses looked ordinary. I could not run Lean, so the proposed lemmas are untested. The proposal rests on the repeated unfold-and-`Function.update_*` pattern, not on any observed simp failure.

findings.problem: `addDirichletUnit b i j` has no canonical pointwise simp lemmas. Every evaluation has to unfold the definition to `Function.update` and then use `Function.update_self` or `Function.update_of_ne`. The target file does this three times: line 55 (`simp only [addDirichletUnit, Function.update_self]`), line 116, and line 120 (`simp [addDirichletUnit, n', hji]`). Line 66 uses `rw [Function.update_of_ne j.property]` on the same unfolded term. This leaks the `Function.update` implementation into proofs. Unfolding also changes the term shape, which is why line 61 needs a manual `change` to restore the intended form. The same pattern appears in other files: `simp [addDirichletUnit, hji]` in Dirichlet/ParameterShift.lean and `simp [addDirichletUnit, h]` in Dirichlet/Average/Deriv.lean. The only simp lemma for the definition is `sum_addDirichletUnit`, so the simp interface is incomplete.
findings.proposed_change: In Dirichlet/ParameterShift.lean, next to `addDirichletUnit`, add `@[simp] theorem addDirichletUnit_self (b : ι → ℂ) (i : ι) : addDirichletUnit b i i = b i + 1 := Function.update_self ..` and `@[simp] theorem addDirichletUnit_of_ne {i j : ι} (h : j ≠ i) (b : ι → ℂ) : addDirichletUnit b i j = b j := Function.update_of_ne h ..`. Both are a one-line unfold plus the corresponding `Function.update` lemma. Then the `hpos'` branches at lines 116 and 120 become `simp [n']` and `simp [n', hji]` with no unfolding. The `simp only [addDirichletUnit, Function.update_self]` at line 55 and the `Function.update_of_ne` rewrite at line 66 can use the new lemmas. The definition then stays folded.
findings.benefit: Proofs about shifted Dirichlet parameters no longer depend on the `Function.update` encoding. The simp normal form `b i + 1` / `b j` is stated once. Call sites can drop the `addDirichletUnit` unfolding hint, which also removes the post-unfolding `change`. The same lemmas would shorten the repeated unfold-then-update pattern in other files, such as ParameterShift.lean and Average/Deriv.lean.

evidence.excerpt: by_cases h : k = i <;> simp [addDirichletUnit, h]
